purpose: Source-backed policy for Oyatie cloud cells and Kubernetes pods: elasticity, auto-healing, auto-rebalancing, scale-to-zero, workload identity, and first-party desired-state authoring. This is local/static planning evidence only.

configuration_authority.kustomize_role: optional low-level patch adapter after CUE export, never canonical policy composition authority
reasoning: CUE gives typed unification, validation, and composable constraints for multi-cell, multi-tenant, multi-region overlays.

Helm is valuable as a package ecosystem and external chart adapter when a chart passes hyperscaler-fit review, but Go-template chart authoring is a weak canonical substrate for policy-heavy first-party cell contracts.
CUE-first lane-owned packages plus generated aggregates reduce shared YAML/Helm merge conflicts and make invalid states unrepresentable before Buck2/Prow admission.

official_sources.establishes: CUE can import Kubernetes schemas, validate Kubernetes resource definitions, and export Kubernetes configuration.
CUE publishes curated Kubernetes modules for typed Kubernetes resource authoring.
Helm charts package Kubernetes resources and remain useful as third-party ecosystem packages.
Helm chart templates use a template language over Kubernetes manifests, so first-party policy-critical state needs an additional typed validation authority if Helm remains in the path.
GKE HPA scales workload replicas horizontally from observed metrics.
GKE VPA recommends or applies CPU and memory request changes for right-sizing workloads.
GKE cluster autoscaler adjusts node-pool capacity and is separate from pod replica autoscaling.
GKE Workload Identity Federation binds Kubernetes ServiceAccounts to short-lived cloud identity instead of node credentials.
AWS recommends Karpenter-style node provisioning from pending pod demand as a scalable cluster capacity pattern.
AWS EKS documents Cluster Autoscaler patterns and tradeoffs for node-group scaling.
AWS EKS identity guidance covers pod identity, IRSA, and restricting pod access to instance metadata credentials.
Shuffle sharding and cell isolation reduce blast radius and noisy-neighbor impact.
KEDA supports event-driven Kubernetes workload scaling, including scale-to-zero patterns when trigger and replica policy permit it.
Kubernetes autoscaling separates workload scaling, resource right-sizing, and cluster capacity scaling concerns.
Pods are ephemeral; controllers recreate or replace them rather than preserving pod identity.
TTL-after-finished supports automatic cleanup for completed Jobs.
Restricted Pod Security is the baseline for least-privilege workload defaults.
NetworkPolicy provides Kubernetes-native pod traffic isolation.
Cloud Native Reference Architecture favors resilient, observable, loosely coupled, automated systems.

elasticity_patterns.decision: HPA owns replica count and VPA owns right-sizing. They must not fight over the same resource signal in auto mode; VPA starts recommend-only unless a workload-specific policy proves safe ownership boundaries.

Node autoscaling is capacity supply, not workload demand policy. The cloud-cell controller may adapt to Karpenter or Cluster Autoscaler patterns, but cell quotas and topology blast walls stay Oyatie-owned.
Scale-to-zero is valid for stateless, event-driven, preview/dev, batch, or async workloads with explicit trigger, idempotency, cold-start SLO, prewarm policy, and no tenant-critical synchronous path.

Pods are disposable. Auto-healing uses controllers, readiness/liveness/startup probes, TTL cleanup, node replacement, PDBs, topology spread, and SLO/error-budget guardrails rather than manual pod deletion.

Cell rebalancing is a control-plane placement problem. Tenant moves require residency/compliance permits, capacity headroom, audit rows, rollback pointers, and rate limits before any migration executes.
All cell workloads use short-lived workload identity, disabled default token mounting unless explicitly required, and blocked node metadata access unless a workload-specific exception is approved.
Autoscaling must respect tenant, account, project, cell, and trust-tier quotas. High parallelism cannot starve control planes, security workloads, or product lanes.
